description: User Intuition runs qualitative research with real people: AI-moderated in-depth interviews, concept tests, and prototype tests.

interface.longDescription:
User Intuition runs qualitative research with real people: AI-moderated in-depth interviews, concept tests, and prototype tests. Teams in consumer goods, retail, and tech use it to learn which packaging claim shoppers notice first, why shoppers switch brands or stores, what happens on the path to purchase, and why new users never activate or customers cancel.

Each interview runs 20–30 minutes and follows up 5–7 levels deep, from what people did to why it matters to them. Findings come back as themes with verbatim quotes linked to the interview they came from.

Recruit from a 4M+ vetted panel, invite your own customers, or recruit B2B audiences to order. Interviews run by voice, video, or chat in 80+ languages. Concept tests can show packaging, claims, ads, or designs; prototype tests can show clickable prototypes, websites, or landing pages. Methodology: https://www.userintuition.ai/methodology/

The assistant drafts the study plan and shows it to you before anything is fielded. A panel launch uses a current cost estimate and needs your explicit approval; recruitment can consume account credits and place a payment-card hold.
defaultPrompt: Test which claim on our new packaging stands out
Interview shoppers about their last grocery trip
Find out why new users never activate

positive.description: Consumer goods: search existing studies for what shoppers said
positive.prompt: Search my studies for what shoppers said about price.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the account's studies with list_studies, then calls search_research with those study IDs. Returns matching findings and verbatim quotes with their source studies, or says nothing matches. Does not create, change, or launch anything.

positive.description: Consumer goods: estimate a panel without launching it
positive.prompt: Estimate 20 interviews in the US at 50% incidence on my most recent study. Do not launch it.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the most recent study with list_studies, then calls estimate_panel with target 20, country US, and incident rate 50. Shows the credit cost, card hold, and timeline. Does not call launch_panel and does not spend credits.

positive.prompt: How many interviews have finished on the study that's currently fielding?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the fielding study with list_studies and reports completed interviews against the target. If no study is fielding, says so. Does not change recruitment.

positive.description: Retail: read findings from a completed study
positive.prompt: What did people say in my most recent completed study? Give me the main themes with quotes.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the most recent completed study and returns its themes with verbatim quotes and their sources. If no report is ready, says so. Never invents quotes or findings.

positive.description: Tech: answer a question from completed research with citations
positive.prompt: Based on my completed studies, why do users drop off during onboarding?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the account's studies, then calls answer_research with the completed study IDs. Answers with numbered citations to the interviews, or says the research does not cover the question. Does not create or launch a study.

negative.prompt: Write a SQL query that counts orders per customer.
Plan a three-day trip to Lisbon.
Summarize this in one sentence: The city council voted on Tuesday to extend library opening hours on weekends starting next month.

publication.release_notes: Version 1.1.0 bundles 21 User Intuition research skills, including consumer goods and retail studies such as concept tests, brand switching, shopper journeys, and usage and attitudes, plus a setup skill that runs after install. The listing and logo are refreshed.
